**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), Chapter 12 §12.2. All examples are newly authored.

## Motivation

Many hyperplanes can separate six easy observations. The maximum-margin principle selects a boundary that leaves the largest geometric separation from the closest training points.

## Derivation and notation

$$
\min_{\boldsymbol w,b}\tfrac12\|\boldsymbol w\|_2^2\quad\text{subject to }y_i(\boldsymbol w^\top\boldsymbol x_i+b)\geq1
$$

Read this model together with the distributional, geometric or optimisation assumptions. An equation without its domain of validity is not a complete explanation.

## Apply it to our running example

For features (distance,items), choose w=(2,0), b=-7. The nearest on-time example at d=3 has y=-1 and score -1, giving functional margin 1. The nearest late example at d=4 has y=+1 and score +1. Since ||w||=2, their geometric distance to the boundary is 1/2 km.

## Constraints and interpretation

This hard-margin optimisation requires linear separability. Soft-margin SVM adds slacks and a penalty C for violations; feature scaling matters for the Euclidean geometry of the margin.

## Your turn

Why can we not simply scale both w and b by ten and claim to have improved the geometric margin?
